title: Reshape embedding schema rollout with client shims and online upcast
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need to change the canonical embedding vector width used by the hosted embeddings endpoint to support new model choices and higher downstream quality. Previous work (ENG-12567/ENG-9221) covered reindex playbooks and client adapters; this ticket designs a zero-downtime rollout strategy that minimizes client changes and limits reindex cost.

Goals:
- Allow index schema to coexist for two widths (e.g., 1536 -> 2048) during a migration window.
- Provide a server-side compatibility shim that accepts old-width requests and upcasts at query time where safe.
- Offer a lightweight client shim SDK to transparently upcast/downcast and normalize scores for reranking integrations.
- Define reindexing strategy for high-throughput customers (shadow indexes, incremental reindex slices).
- Measure latency and cost impact and create automated rerouting policies for capacity-sensitive tiers.

Approach summary:
1) Schema metadata: add an immutable index field vector_width (integer) and a schema_version string for each index. Indexes created before the migration keep vector_width=1536, new indexes use 2048. Search paths will consult vector_width to determine compatible lookup strategy.
2) Server compatibility shim: implement on-read upcast path that pads vectors with model-derived projection or zeros and runs nearest-neighbor search against mixed-width index shards. This avoids immediate reindex for read-heavy workloads.
3) Client shim SDK: publish a small adapter (JS/Python) that negotiates preferred_width with the server; it will optionally project client embeddings on the fly to the requested width and normalize cosine scores to pre-migration baselines. Docs will include a single-line opt-in flag to enable shim behavior.
4) Reindexing options: provide three patterns in the playbook: (A) Shadow reindex (create new index, sync deltas, then swap), (B) Rolling slice reindex (slice corpus by id ranges and swap slices), (C) On-demand reindex for low-traffic customers. Provide cost estimates per 1M items for each pattern.
5) Reranking compatibility: ensure rerank endpoint accepts multi-width candidate batches; the reranker will run a normalization layer that accounts for differences in vector norm and dim before passing to the ranker model.
6) Telemetry and SLOs: add metrics for average query latency per width, upcast fallbacks per-minute, and reindex progress percent. Create dashboard and alert (e.g., upcast rate > 5% for more than 15m).

Operational constraints and trade-offs:
- Upcasting at query time increases CPU/GPU overhead and adds tail latency; we'll gate default behavior by customer tier and add a cost-warning header.
- Projection-based upcast (learned linear projection) yields better retrieval quality than zero-padding but requires storing projection matrices per-model and extra storage.
- Full reindex is the only way to eliminate compatibility overhead; provide clear cost/time guidance.

Deliverables:
- Server-side compatibility shim implementation (runtime-1.19 feature flag).
- Client shim SDKs (python/js) with opt-in negotiation protocol.
- Reindex playbook and cost calculator doc.
- Dashboard and alerting for migration signals.
- Compatibility test suite and benchmark results comparing padding vs projection approaches.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes index metadata (vector_width, schema_version) on index describe API
Compatibility shim can answer mixed-width queries with no functional errors and exposes upcast rate metric
Client shim SDKs available in PyPI/NPM with migration docs and single-line opt-in flag
Reindex playbook published with sample cost estimates and three recommended patterns
Benchmarks show <=10% median latency increase for upcast path under typical load (with documented tail latency)
Rerank endpoint accepts candidate batches with mixed widths and returns normalized scores matching post-reindex baseline within acceptable delta (TBD)
